items.stem: The quadratic $f(x)=(x+5)^{2}-3$ is already written in vertex form. What is the vertex of its graph?
items.hint: Vertex form is $a(x-h)^{2}+k$, so ask which value of $x$ makes the squared bracket equal to zero.
worked: Vertex form is $f(x)=a(x-h)^{2}+k$, and the vertex is the point $(h,k)$.
The constant sitting outside the square is $k=-3$.

items.stem: Expand $f(x)=(x-6)^{2}+2$ and write it in the standard form $ax^{2}+bx+c$.
items.hint: Rewrite $(x-6)^{2}$ as the product $(x-6)(x-6)$ and multiply it out fully before you add the $2$.

items.stem: A student rewrites $f(x)=x^{2}-8x+3$ first as $f(x)=(x^{2}-8x+16)+3$ and then as $f(x)=(x-4)^{2}+3$. Which statement about this work is true?
items.hint: Test both expressions at $x=0$; if they are the same function they must produce the same output.
worked: Half of $-8$ is $-4$, and $(-4)^{2}=16$, so $16$ is the right number to build the square.
But inserting $16$ makes the expression $16$ larger than $f$, so $16$ must be taken back out: $x^{2}-8x+3=(x^{2}-8x+16)+3-16$.

options.text: It is wrong: the $16$ must be taken back out, so $f(x)=(x-4)^{2}-13$.
It is wrong: the square should be $(x+4)^{2}$, so $f(x)=(x+4)^{2}-13$.
It is wrong: the constant must be adjusted by $+16$, so $f(x)=(x-4)^{2}+19$.

items.stem: The parabola $f(x)=2x^{2}-12x+5$ opens upward, so $f$ has a minimum. What is the minimum value of $f$?
items.hint: Locate the vertex first, either by completing the square or with $x=\dfrac{-b}{2a}$, then decide which coordinate of that point the question is asking for.
worked: Factor the leading $2$ out of the $x$ terms: $f(x)=2(x^{2}-6x)+5$.
Half of $-6$ is $-3$ and $(-3)^{2}=9$; adding $9$ inside the bracket adds $2(9)=18$ to the whole function, so subtract $18$ outside.
The vertex is $(3,-13)$, so the smallest output is $-13$.

items.hint: Factor the $-1$ out of the $x$ terms before completing the square, and keep track of what that $-1$ does to the number you insert inside the bracket.
worked: Half of $-6$ is $-3$ and $(-3)^{2}=9$; the $9$ placed inside the bracket is multiplied by $-1$, so it lowers the function by $9$ and must be added back outside.
Since $a=-1$ the parabola opens downward, so the vertex $(3,5)$ is the highest point: the maximum value is $5$, reached at $x=3$.

options.text: $f$ has a maximum value of $-13$, reached at $x=3$.
$f$ has a maximum value of $5$, reached at $x=3$.
$f$ has a maximum value of $5$, reached at $x=-3$.
$f$ has a maximum value of $3$, reached at $x=5$.
